question: Who started the first newspaper in India? (RRB NTPC CBT-I (11/03/2021) Shift 1)
options: Derk Sauer
John Campbell
Edward Mallet
James A Hickey
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is James A Hickey

Explanation:
The first newspaper in India was the Bengal Gazette (also known as the Calcutta General Advertiser), started by James Augustus Hickey in 1780. It was a weekly English newspaper published during the British East India Company rule. Hickey printed it on his own press and it included trade news, general news, and advertisements. The newspaper criticized the colonial government, which led to its eventual closure and Hickey's imprisonment. The first Hindi newspaper in India was Udant Martand, started in 1826 by Jugal Kishore Shukla.

☛ Place of publication of Bengal Gazette → Calcutta
question_hi: भारत में पहला समाचार पत्र किसने शुरू किया था? (RRB NTPC CBT-I (11/03/2021) Shift 1)

solution_hi:

Explanation:
भारत में पहला समाचार पत्र बंगाल गजट (जिसे कलकत्ता जनरल एडवरटाइजर भी कहा जाता है) था, जिसे जेम्स ऑगस्टस हिकी ने 1780 में शुरू किया था। यह एक साप्ताहिक अंग्रेजी अखबार था जो ब्रिटिश ईस्ट इंडिया कंपनी के शासन के दौरान प्रकाशित हुआ। हिकी ने इसे अपने स्वयं के प्रेस पर छापा और इसमें व्यापार, समाचार और विज्ञापन शामिल थे। इस अखबार ने औपनिवेशिक सरकार की आलोचना की, जिसके कारण बाद में इसे बंद कर दिया गया और हिकी को जेल भेज दिया गया। भारत में पहला हिंदी समाचार पत्र उदंत मार्तंड था, जो 1826 में जुगल किशोर शुक्ल ने शुरू किया था।

question: In which city was Gandhiji informed about the problems in Champaran and invited to visit the place?  (RRB NTPC CBT-I (14/03/2021) Shift 1)
options: Lucknow
Delhi
Patna
Ahmedabad
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Lucknow

Explanation:
Gandhiji was informed about the problems in Champaran and invited to visit the place in the city of Lucknow. In 1917, Gandhi attended a meeting in Lucknow where he met Rajkumar Shukla, a peasant leader. Shukla told him about the oppression of farmers under the indigo cultivation system in Champaran and urged him to come and help the peasants. This led to Gandhi's visit to Champaran, where he successfully resolved the farmers' issues through his method of Satyagraha. This event is considered Gandhi's first successful Satyagraha movement in India and marked a significant turning point in the Indian freedom struggle.

question: The 1857 revolt at Lucknow was led by: (RRB NTPC CBT-I (03/03/2021) Shift 2)
options: Vir Savarkar
Tatya Tope
Kunwar Singh
Begum Hazrat Mahal
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Begum Hazrat Mahal

Explanation:
The 1857 revolt at Lucknow was led by Begum Hazrat Mahal, the wife of Nawab Wajid Ali Shah of Awadh. After the British exiled the Nawab to Bengal, she took charge of the rebellion. She declared her son Birjis Qadir as the ruler and fought against the British. The British faced significant resistance in Lucknow before finally suppressing the revolt. Eventually, Begum Hazrat Mahal had to flee to Nepal, where she sought asylum. She remains an iconic symbol of women's participation in India's freedom struggle. Her leadership in the revolt of 1857 is a testament to the spirit of resistance against colonial rule.

Explanation:

question: Wood's Dispatch was concerned with which of the following reforms? (RRB NTPC CBT-I (03/03/2021) Shift 2)
options: Railways
Education
Irrigation
Industry
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Education

Explanation:
Wood's Dispatch was a historic document issued in 1854 during British rule, which was concerned with educational reforms in India. It is named after Sir Charles Wood, who was the President of the Board of Control at that time. This dispatch laid the foundation of the modern education system in India, emphasizing English medium education, establishment of universities, and teacher training. As a result, the universities of Calcutta, Bombay, and Madras were established in 1857. Wood's Dispatch aimed to propagate Western education and prepare Indians for administrative services. It is a significant milestone in the field of education, whereas railways, irrigation, and industry were not related to it.

☛ During which rule did Wood's Dispatch come? → British rule
question_hi: वुड्स डिस्पैच निम्नलिखित में से किस सुधार से संबंधित था? (RRB NTPC CBT-I (03/03/2021) Shift 2)

सिंचाई

Explanation:
वुड्स डिस्पैच 1854 में ब्रिटिश शासन के दौरान जारी किया गया एक ऐतिहासिक दस्तावेज था, जो भारत में शिक्षा सुधारों से संबंधित था। इसे सर चार्ल्स वुड के नाम पर जाना जाता है, जो उस समय बोर्ड ऑफ कंट्रोल के अध्यक्ष थे। इस डिस्पैच ने भारत में आधुनिक शिक्षा प्रणाली की नींव रखी, जिसमें अंग्रेजी माध्यम से शिक्षा, विश्वविद्यालयों की स्थापना, और शिक्षक प्रशिक्षण पर जोर दिया गया। इसके परिणामस्वरूप कलकत्ता, बंबई और मद्रास विश्वविद्यालयों की स्थापना 1857 में हुई। वुड्स डिस्पैच का उद्देश्य पाश्चात्य शिक्षा का प्रसार करना और भारतीयों को प्रशासनिक सेवाओं के लिए तैयार करना था। यह शिक्षा के क्षेत्र में एक महत्वपूर्ण मील का पत्थर है, जबकि रेलवे, सिंचाई और उद्योग से इसका कोई संबंध नहीं है।

question: Which of the following statements with reference to the Indian Freedom Struggle is INCORRECT?  (RRB NTPC CBT-I (24/07/2021) Shift 1)

Sheikh Mujibur Rahman played an important role in the freedom struggle of India.

Explanation:
Sheikh Mujibur Rahman was the founding leader of Bangladesh and a key figure in East Pakistan's independence movement, having no association with the Indian freedom struggle. The Mutiny of 1857 is regarded as the First War of Independence. The Simon Commission arrived in Bombay in 1928, facing widespread protests and 'Simon Go Back' slogans. question: Which of the following statements with respect to the Jallianwala Bagh incident is INCORRECT?  (RRB NTPC CBT-I (24/07/2021) Shift 1)
options: The Jallianwala Bagh was a result of the Rowlatt Act of March 1919, which authorised the government to imprison without a trial.
The incident took place on 13 April 1919, when the publlic gathered at Jallianwala Bagh with an agenda.
The Jallianwala Bagh incident was followed by the Chauri Chaura incident, where a large group of protesters clashed with the police.
Brigadier-General Dyer opened fire at the people gathered, without giving any notice.
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is The Jallianwala Bagh incident was followed by the Chauri Chaura incident

Explanation:
The Jallianwala Bagh massacre occurred on 13 April 1919, when Brigadier-General Dyer opened fire on unarmed civilians without warning. It was a result of the Rowlatt Act (March 1919), which authorised the government to imprison without trial. The Chauri Chaura incident took place on 4 February 1922 during the Non-Cooperation Movement, when protesters set fire to a police station. Thus, Jallianwala Bagh preceded Chauri Chaura, not the other way around. All other statements are correct.

☛ Who ordered the firing → Brigadier-General Dyer
☛ Act that triggered the incident → Rowlatt Act (1919)
☛ Date of Chauri Chaura incident → 4 February 1922
☛ Movement withdrawn after Chauri Chaura → Non-Cooperation Movement
question_hi: जलियांवाला बाग हत्याकांड के संबंध में निम्नलिखित में से कौन सा कथन गलत है? (RRB NTPC CBT-I (24/07/2021) Shift 1)

यह घटना 13 अप्रैल 1919 को हुई, जब जनता एक एजेंडे के साथ जलियांवाला बाग में इकट्ठी हुई थी।
जलियांवाला बाग की घटना चौरी चौरा की घटना के बाद हुई थी, जिसमें प्रदर्शनकारियों का एक बड़ा समूह पुलिस के साथ भिड़ गया था।
ब्रिगेडियर-जनरल डायर ने बिना किसी सूचना के इकट्ठे हुए लोगों पर गोलियां चलवा दीं।
solution_hi:
Solution: सही उत्तर है जलियांवाला बाग की घटना चौरी चौरा की घटना के बाद हुई थी

question: "Swaraj is my birthright and I shall have it." Who is this famous statement? (RPF SI 2018 (16/01/2019) Shift 2)
options: Bhagat Singh
Sardar Vallabh Bhai Patel
Bal Gangadhar Tilak
Mahatma Gandhi
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Bal Gangadhar Tilak

Explanation:
The famous quote 'Swaraj is my birthright and I shall have it' was proclaimed by Bal Gangadhar Tilak. He was a prominent nationalist leader, social reformer, and a key figure in the Indian freedom struggle. Revered as Lokmanya, he made the demand for Swaraj the central theme of Indian politics. Tilak popularized mass celebrations like Ganesh Chaturthi and Shivaji Jayanti to unite people against British rule. He authored the book Gita Rahasya, interpreting the Bhagavad Gita in a nationalist context. The British government exiled him to Mandalay (Burma) from 1908 to 1914 on charges of sedition. Tilak's slogan became a rallying cry for the independence movement, inspiring generations of freedom fighters.

question: In which year was Awadh formally annexed to the British Empire? (RPF Constable 2024 (18/03/2025) Shift 1)

1856

IPTA played a crucial role in connecting the cultural movement with the nationalist movement, fostering a sense of unity and resistance against colonial oppression.

options_hi: ब्रिटिश शिक्षा नीति को प्रोत्साहित किया

solution_hi:
Solution: सही उत्तर है कला के माध्यम से असहमति व्यक्त की

Explanation:
इंडियन पीपुल्स थिएटर एसोसिएशन (IPTA) की स्थापना 1942 में हुई थी। इसका मुख्य उद्देश्य ब्रिटिश शासन के खिलाफ जनजागरूकता फैलाना और सामाजिक-राजनीतिक मुद्दों को उठाना था। IPTA ने नाटक, गीत और नृत्य के माध्यम से ब्रिटिश नीतियों की आलोचना की और स्वतंत्रता संग्राम को समर्थन दिया। यह संगठन मार्क्सवादी विचारधारा से प्रभावित था और इसमें बलराज साहनी, के.ए. अब्बास जैसे कलाकार शामिल थे। IPTA ने कला को राजनीतिक अभिव्यक्ति का माध्यम बनाकर जनता में राष्ट्रीय चेतना जगाई।
